title: StudioBrain Provider File
description: How to talk to a generation backend. Drop *.provider.yaml in _Providers/ (project) or templates/Providers/ (catalog) — never a single providers.yaml. Unknown backends are a second tiny file — no new Rust crate. Engine/framework choice + default weight rows per device/build live in *.platform.yaml (schemas/platform.json), not in divergent code (SBAI-7974).

route.description: aigateway = StudioBrain's Cloudflare AI Gateway route for BrainBits or BYOK; direct = the provider/local endpoint with no BrainBits billing.

starter.description: Whether new projects install this catalog provider automatically. Only hosted aigateway providers may be starters.

wire.description: Protocol-level dialect this backend speaks (openai-compat, anthropic, …). NOT the execution engine — that is `engine.category` (MM v2 taxonomy: local_inprocess / local_spawned / lan_endpoint / distributed / cloud_provider / llm_router). Do not conflate the two (SBAI-7974). process = desktop/LAN CLI (Blender, UVR). Cloud workers must 501 process and localhost base_url. dashscope = Alibaba DashScope native API, which is NOT openai-compatible; its compatible-mode endpoint (/compatible-mode/v1) can instead be used with wire: openai-compat. in-app = executes inside the client app via the ai-sdk on-device executor (WebGPU/WASM, no network hop); same doctrine as process -- cloud workers must 501 it.

engine.description: Preferred-or-required execution engine (SBAI-7974). Reuses model-manager engines.schema.json v2 taxonomy_category. Shorthand string = category with requirement=preferred. Distinct from `wire` (protocol) and from in-app `runtime` (which in-app engine loads the weights).

limits.description: Provider-level caps passed through and honored by every executor type. Settings and platform.yaml overlay these at runtime; do not hard-code the same numbers at call sites.

provides.description: Kebab-case capability tags (e.g. llm-chat, tts, voice-clone, image-gen, video-gen, music-gen, 3d-gen, audio-stems, media-convert). Capability matching (workflow step substitution) and marketplace filtering consume this.

client_direct.description: Curated knowledge that a browser may call this provider directly (CORS). Absent means unknown — the designed default for providers that do not publish a CORS policy.

runtime.description: in-app only -- the DEFAULT engine the in-app executor uses to run this provider's weights on-device. A weights row may override it with its own 'runtime' (SBAI-7844): one in-app provider can hold tiers for more than one engine, and the executor loads the row it selected, not the provider header.

models.description: Where the app pulls the provider's live model list, and the cache interval.

weights.description: Static per-device weight rows for wire:in-app providers -- distinct from 'models', which is live-list discovery. Each row is one downloadable weight variant the in-app executor may select based on detected device capability.

id.description: Slug identifying this weight row. '/' is allowed so rows can be namespaced by provider, e.g. on-device/gemma-4-e2b-it-q4f16-webgpu. Namespacing is what lets a money-leak guard reject an on-device id ('on-device/*') by prefix instead of by an ever-growing list of bare slugs.

source.description: Weight source, conventionally 'huggingface://<repo-id>' (scripts/validate.py WARNs on other forms rather than hard-failing, so alternate sources can still ship; an empty source is a hard error).

dtype.description: Tier dtype AND execution prerequisite: q4f16/fp16 rows need the WebGPU shader-f16 feature, and q4 has no WASM kernel. For a multi-module model this is the tier label and f16 gate; dtype_map carries the per-module truth.

dtype_map.description: Per-module dtype overrides for multi-file models (Florence-2, Gemma multimodal, FastVLM-class): module name -> dtype, e.g. {embed_tokens: fp16, vision_encoder: fp16, decoder_model_merged: q4f16}. Modules quantize very differently -- q4 only touches MatMul, so it is useless on a conv-heavy vision encoder -- and picking the mix is a catalog decision, not something each client should re-derive.

runtime.description: Which in-app engine loads THIS row, overriding the provider-level runtime (SBAI-7844). Per row rather than per provider because the on-device provider now holds transformers.js tiers and litert-lm tiers side by side. Omitted, the row is a transformers.js row -- which is what every row that predates this field is, so absence must never be reinterpreted.

file.description: One named weight FILE inside the repo, WITH its extension, e.g. 'gemma-4-E2B-it-web.litertlm'. Required for runtime: litert-lm, where a repo publishes several mutually incompatible .litertlm builds side by side (-web, -gpu, and one per NPU vendor) and only the -web one runs in a browser -- guessing would download gigabytes of the wrong build. Distinct from model_file_name, which is transformers.js's EXTENSIONLESS model_file_name for picking one graph out of a repo's onnx/ directory.

model_file_name.description: Load only this graph out of a multi-tower repo, e.g. 'vision_model' for a SigLIP row that ships the vision tower alone and scores against precomputed text embeddings. Maps to transformers.js model_file_name.

taxonomy.description: id of the taxonomy this row scores against (taxonomies/*.yaml). Zero-shot rows only.

taxonomy_embeddings.description: Repo-relative path to the precomputed text-embedding artifact for this row's model tier (taxonomies/*.embeddings.json). Per-TIER, not per-taxonomy: embedding dimensionality differs between tiers, so a row must never point at another tier's artifact. scripts/validate.py checks the file exists and that its taxonomy stamp is current.

min_ram_gb.description: Minimum host RAM in GiB. Same field as schemas/_limits.json; honored by every executor type.

min_vram_gb.description: Minimum GPU VRAM in GiB. Same field as schemas/_limits.json; honored by every executor type.

approx_download_mb.description: Approximate download size in MiB. Same field as schemas/_limits.json; honored by every executor type.

revision.description: Immutable pinned commit SHA this row was verified against -- huggingface.co/api/models/<repo> 'sha' at pin time, NEVER a branch or tag. 'main'/'latest' are moving targets: SBAI-7842's first-party mirror guarantees a pinned revision stays available forever, which only holds if the catalog actually pins one. scripts/verify_mirror_manifest.py hard-refuses any row whose revision does not match this 40-hex pattern (SBAI-7881).

license.description: SPDX-ish id of the redistribution license for this row's weights, as declared on the HF repo (or its unambiguous base_model when the ONNX/GGUF conversion repo carries no license tag of its own). Only OSI-approved, redistributable licenses may appear here -- scripts/verify_mirror_manifest.py refuses any id outside this enum by construction, which is what keeps a repo like onnx-community/FastVLM-0.5B-ONNX (apple-amlr, not OSI) out of this catalog at the schema level rather than by comment discipline alone (SBAI-7726's on-device.provider.yaml doctrine). Extend the enum only after confirming a new license is genuinely OSI-approved and redistributable.

license_artifact.description: Repo-relative path to the full license text mirrored alongside this row's weight objects (e.g. licenses/apache-2.0.txt). scripts/verify_mirror_manifest.py checks the file exists; the R2 mirror (SBAI-7882) publishes it next to the weight objects at '<mirror_path>LICENSE.txt' so a downloaded weight is never separated from its license.

mirror_path.description: R2 object-key PREFIX this row's files mirror to, deterministic from source + revision (on-device/<owner>__<repo>/<revision>/ -- '/' in the HF repo id becomes '__' since R2 keys are flat strings, not a filesystem). Each entry in 'files' publishes at '<mirror_path><files[i].name>'. Declared explicitly rather than derived at consume time so SBAI-7882 (provisions it), SBAI-7883 (app fetches it), and SBAI-7884 (model-manager fetches it) read one field instead of three independent re-derivations of the same string.

size.description: Exact total byte size of this row's 'files' (sum). Distinct from approx_download_mb, which stays the pre-existing rounded-MB, human-facing figure -- 'size' is what scripts/verify_mirror_manifest.py checksums against and what a downloader uses for exact progress/space-check math.

files.description: Every constituent weight/module file this row downloads, each independently checksummed -- the ONNX graph(s) and their external-data shard(s) (e.g. decoder_model_merged_q4.onnx + decoder_model_merged_q4.onnx_data), or the single .litertlm file. Deliberately excludes tokenizer/config sidecars -- those are small, non-weight files outside this contract's scope (SBAI-7881); a future ticket may extend coverage to them. scripts/verify_mirror_manifest.py sums files[].size and refuses drift from the row's 'size'.

name.description: Bare filename, no directory (e.g. decoder_model_merged_q4.onnx_data). The mirror does not preserve the source repo's directory structure -- 'mirror_path' is the only prefix a consumer needs.

sha256.description: Exact content hash, sourced from the HF tree API's lfs.oid for this file at 'revision' (verified via huggingface.co/api/models/<repo>/tree/<revision>?recursive=true). scripts/verify_mirror_manifest.py checks format/presence only -- it does not download multi-gigabyte files in CI; 'scripts/verify_mirror_manifest.py --verify-remote' re-fetches this from HF as an opt-in maintenance check outside the CI gate.

size.description: Exact byte size of this one file, from the same HF tree API lookup as sha256.

context_length.description: Model context window in tokens for this weight row. Consumed as ModelGateway.contextLength so the orchestrator compacts against the real window instead of a hard-coded default -- a tier that clamps lower for memory must say so here.

max_output_tokens.description: Upper bound on tokens this row should generate in one turn; the executor caps max_new_tokens at this value. Alias of limits.max_tokens — if both are set they must agree (validate.py errors on disagreement).

max_tokens.description: Canonical generation-cap name (SBAI-7974). Alias of max_output_tokens. Prefer this in platform.yaml / settings overlays; weight rows may keep max_output_tokens.

tools.description: Whether this model reliably emits tool calls. False means the executor must not pass tool definitions into the chat template -- a model that cannot call tools but is handed them tends to hallucinate the call syntax as prose.

thinking.description: Thinking/reasoning mode support: 'none' = the row has no thinking mode (never enable it), 'optional' = caller may request it, 'always' = the model always thinks and the flag is forced on.

capability.description: Capability this weight row serves, e.g. llm-chat or embeddings.

default.description: Preferred row for its capability/device tier when multiple rows qualify.

fallback.description: Reduced-capability row offered only when no default-tier row is admissible.

experimental.description: Row is offered but not yet hardened (e.g. near a WASM memory ceiling).

pricing.description: Dynamic price feed or static per-model table. Prefer a real endpoint; static tables rot. 'operand' is the separate, typed, provider-neutral price the marketplace approx-cost badge multiplies by a canvas's step_count (SBAI-7675) -- distinct from 'table', which is an unstructured per-model blob with no consumer contract. A provider that omits 'operand' has UNKNOWN pricing to the marketplace: consumers must render unknown/unavailable, and must never default a missing operand to 0 (0 means 'confirmed free', which is a different fact).

operand.description: Static price operand: approx_cost = operand.amount * canvas.step_count when unit is 'per-step' (other units are informational only until a per-unit consumption estimator exists -- out of scope for SBAI-7675). Only declare this for a price attributable to a real, current vendor rate card. Never estimate or invent one -- a provider with no trustworthy source must omit 'operand' entirely rather than guess.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code. Only USD is modeled this cycle -- add codes here (not free-text) when a second currency is actually needed.

unit.description: What one 'amount' buys. 'per-step' is the only unit the step_count multiplier consumes directly today; the others are declared for forward compatibility with a future per-unit estimator.

amount.description: Positive price in 'currency' per 'unit'. There is deliberately no zero/free spelling here: a free provider expresses that by omitting 'pricing' entirely (unknown-not-zero), so the marketplace can never conflate 'we don't know the price' with 'this is confirmed free'.

billing.description: byok = user's own key, unmetered; brainbits = our preset key, metered. Local/device providers omit the field (free when it is the user's device or the user's key).

chat.description: Chat-routing hints so ai-sdk's hardcoded KNOWN_PROVIDERS table can be codegen'd from the catalog. Values mirror ProviderRecord in the ai-sdk provider registry.

nativeChatPath.description: Native chat path, e.g. chat/completions or v1/messages.

modelPrefixes.description: Model-id prefixes used for provider inference, e.g. [gpt-, claude-].

slots.description: What this backend accepts and emits. Workflow edges only connect matching modalities.

requires.description: Runtime requirements. 'wire: process' and localhost base_url imply platforms containing 'desktop'; auth.env should be mirrored in requires.env.

base_url.description: Empty/omitted means the platform default (AI Gateway / local model-manager) -- EXCEPT for wire: in-app, which has no URL at all: consumers must branch on wire before applying any base_url default, or an on-device request silently becomes a metered cloud call.

bootstrap.description: Environment variable aliases for base_url override. Enables transparent failover between compatible endpoints (e.g., OLLAMA_URL -> LITELLM_URL -> MODEL_MANAGER_URL).

base_url_env.description: Primary environment variable for base URL override (e.g., OLLAMA_URL)

base_url_env_aliases.description: Fallback environment variables tried in order if primary is unset

mm_cloud.description: Cloud-specific routing metadata for model-manager. Used when the same provider YAML is consumed by both desktop (local) and cloud (metered API) contexts.

api_key_env.description: Environment variable containing the cloud API key

auth.description: header/scheme/env describe key auth. scheme 'oauth2' is RESERVED (SBAI-7619): authorize_url / token_url / scopes / client_name may be declared, but no OAuth flow is implemented this cycle and no catalog provider uses it yet.

headers.description: Static headers sent with every request, e.g. {"anthropic-version": "2023-06-01"}. Auth headers belong in the auth block, not here.
